title: Best Countertop Ice Makers 2026: Gevi vs Frigidaire vs Euhomy vs Igloo
description: Five countertop ice makers compared on ice type (bullet vs nugget), production speed, capacity, noise, and price — from the budget Igloo to the chewable-nugget Gevi.
lede: A countertop ice maker is the small appliance people don't know they want until a hot summer or a party reveals how slow and small a freezer's ice trays really are. The catch: 'ice maker' covers everything from quick clear bullets to coveted chewable nugget ice, and they're nothing alike.

sections.heading: Top pick: Gevi Household Bullet Ice Maker
paragraphs: The Gevi Household Ice Maker is the best countertop ice maker for most people because it makes ice fast, in useful quantity, in a compact, affordable, no-plumbing package. It's a bullet/cylinder ice maker — you just pour water into the reservoir (no water line needed), press a button, and it produces a batch of ice in around 6-8 minutes, churning out a generous amount per day, far faster and more plentiful than freezer trays. It's self-contained and portable, fits on a countertop, and lets you choose ice cube size (smaller for faster, larger for longer-lasting), making it ideal for everyday drinks, gatherings, and topping up a cooler.

Its appeal is the combination of speed, convenience, and value: no installation or plumbing (just add water and plug in), quick batches so you're not waiting long for the first ice, a clear window to watch the level, and an automatic shut-off when the basket is full. Gevi is one of the most popular countertop ice maker brands precisely because units like this reliably deliver fast, abundant ice for everyday use at an accessible price. For someone who just wants plenty of ice quickly without plumbing or a big freezer, it's the benchmark.

The honest caveats: bullet ice makers produce cloudy, hollow-cylinder ice (perfectly good for chilling drinks but not crystal-clear cocktail ice), the ice isn't frozen in long-term storage so it slowly melts in the basket if not used (the melt-water recycles to make more ice, but it won't keep ice frozen for hours like a freezer), and it's not the chewable nugget ice some people crave. But for fast, abundant, convenient everyday ice at a great price, the Gevi bullet maker is the default.

sections.heading: Best nugget ice and best value nugget: Gevi Nugget and Euhomy
paragraphs: The Gevi Nugget Ice Maker is the pick for the holy grail of ice — soft, chewable 'nugget' or 'pebble' ice, the kind beloved from Sonic and Chick-fil-A. Nugget ice makers produce small, soft, chewable nuggets of ice made from compacted ice flakes, which chill drinks fast, absorb flavour, and are genuinely fun and satisfying to chew — a cult favourite that people specifically buy a dedicated machine for. The Gevi nugget maker delivers this chewable ice at home in a countertop unit (no plumbing, just add water), and it's a more affordable way into nugget ice than the famous premium nugget machines. It's the standout for anyone who specifically wants that soft, chewable, sonic-style ice. The trade-offs: nugget ice makers are more expensive, slower, and more complex than simple bullet makers, and they have more parts to maintain — but for nugget-ice devotees, no bullet maker substitutes.

The Euhomy Countertop Ice Maker is the value all-rounder, a popular, well-reviewed bullet-style ice maker that competes closely with the Gevi on fast, abundant ice at an affordable price. It offers quick ice production (a batch in well under 10 minutes), good daily output, selectable cube sizes, no-plumbing operation, and a self-contained countertop design, often at a competitive or lower price than other bullet makers. Euhomy is a frequent best-seller in the category, and for someone choosing between budget-to-mid bullet ice makers, it's effectively interchangeable with the Gevi bullet — worth comparing on current price and capacity. It's the sensible value pick when it undercuts the alternatives while delivering the same fast, plentiful everyday ice.

Choose between them by what ice you want. The Gevi Nugget wins decisively if you specifically crave soft, chewable nugget/pebble ice and will pay more for a dedicated machine. The Euhomy wins as an affordable, fast, abundant everyday bullet ice maker (like the Gevi bullet). The Gevi Nugget is the chewable-ice splurge; the Euhomy the value bullet workhorse.

sections.heading: The portable/RV pick and the budget pick: Frigidaire and Igloo
paragraphs: The Frigidaire EFIC108 is the popular, trusted-brand pick that balances reliable performance, a recognisable name, and a compact, often stylish design (in fun colours). It's a bullet-style countertop ice maker delivering fast batches, good daily output, selectable ice sizes, and no-plumbing operation, with the reassurance of the Frigidaire name and a track record as a best-seller. It's a strong middle-ground choice for someone who wants dependable, fast countertop ice from a familiar brand, often available in colours that look good on a counter or in an RV, dorm, office, or kitchen. It performs comparably to the Gevi and Euhomy bullet makers, so the draw is the brand trust and the design/colour options at a competitive price.

The Igloo Portable Ice Maker is the budget and portability pick — Igloo (the cooler brand) makes accessible, often very affordable countertop/portable ice makers ideal for taking ice-making on the go (RVs, boats, camping with power, tailgates, parties) or for a cheap home unit. It does the core bullet-ice job — fast batches, no plumbing, compact and lightweight, selectable sizes — at a budget-friendly price, with the portability and casual appeal Igloo is known for, often in fun colours. The build and longevity won't match premium units, but for an affordable, portable ice maker for occasional, casual, or on-the-go use, it's the value standout. It's the pick for someone who wants cheap, portable ice rather than a permanent kitchen fixture.

Choose between them by priority. The Frigidaire wins on trusted-brand reliability and stylish design for a dependable everyday countertop unit. The Igloo wins on the lowest price and portability for casual, on-the-go, or budget use. The Frigidaire is the trusted everyday pick; the Igloo the cheap, portable, take-anywhere pick.

sections.heading: How to choose: ice type, speed, capacity, noise, and use
paragraphs: Decide the ice type first, because it's the biggest difference between machines. Bullet ice (Gevi bullet, Euhomy, Frigidaire, Igloo) is the standard fast countertop ice — cloudy, hollow cylinders that chill drinks well, made quickly and cheaply; it's what most countertop ice makers produce and is fine for everyday drinks, coolers, and parties. Nugget/pebble ice (Gevi Nugget) is the soft, chewable, sonic-style ice that's a cult favourite — it chills fast, absorbs flavour, and is satisfying to chew, but the machines are pricier, slower, and more complex. Clear ice (from premium clear-ice makers, less common in countertop units) is the crystal-clear cocktail ice. Decide whether you want fast cheap everyday ice (bullet) or specifically crave chewable nugget ice (and will pay for a dedicated machine) — this single choice narrows your options most.

Match production speed and capacity to your needs, and understand storage. Countertop ice makers are about fast, continuous production rather than storage: most make a batch in roughly 6-10 minutes and produce a stated amount per 24 hours, but the basket holds a limited amount and — crucially — is not a freezer, so the ice slowly melts if not used (the melt-water usually recycles back to make more ice). This means they're excellent for on-demand and same-day ice (a party, a hot afternoon, filling drinks and coolers throughout the day) but won't store a stockpile frozen for later like a freezer — for that you transfer the ice to your freezer. Match the daily output and batch speed to whether you need a steady on-demand supply (most units suffice) or large volumes for entertaining (look at the higher-output models), and don't expect it to keep ice frozen for hours unused.

Weigh noise, size, and intended use. Ice makers run a compressor and are audibly noisy in operation (the ice dropping and compressor cycling), so consider placement if noise bothers you (a kitchen is fine; a quiet open-plan living space less so) — nugget makers and some units are quieter or louder, so check reviews if noise matters. Size and portability vary: compact bullet makers fit a counter and many are light enough to move (Igloo emphasises portability for RVs and travel), while nugget makers are typically larger and heavier. Consider where you'll use it — a permanent kitchen fixture, an RV or boat, a home bar, an office — and choose the size, portability, and output to match. Also factor in maintenance: all ice makers need periodic cleaning and descaling to stay hygienic and efficient. Buy for the ice type you want, with the speed and output for your use, accepting the noise and that it makes ice on demand rather than storing it frozen.

faqs.q: What's the difference between bullet ice and nugget ice makers?
faqs.a: They make completely different ice and suit different priorities. Bullet ice makers (like the Gevi bullet, Euhomy, Frigidaire, and Igloo) produce the standard countertop ice — small, cloudy, hollow cylinders ('bullets') — quickly (a batch in roughly 6-10 minutes), cheaply, and in good quantity; this ice chills drinks well and is perfect for everyday use, parties, and coolers, and bullet makers are the affordable, fast, popular default. Nugget ice makers (like the Gevi Nugget) produce soft, chewable 'nugget' or 'pebble' ice made from compacted ice flakes — the cult-favourite Sonic/Chick-fil-A style ice that chills drinks fast, absorbs flavour, and is genuinely satisfying to chew. People specifically seek out nugget machines because no bullet maker can replicate that soft, chewable texture. The trade-offs: nugget ice makers are more expensive, slower to produce ice, larger, and more complex with more parts to maintain. So choose a bullet ice maker if you want fast, abundant, affordable everyday ice for chilling drinks; choose a nugget ice maker if you specifically love chewable pebble ice and are willing to pay more and wait a bit longer for it. The ice-type decision is the most important one when buying.

faqs.q: Do countertop ice makers keep ice frozen, or does it melt?
faqs.a: They do not keep ice frozen long-term — this is the single most misunderstood thing about countertop ice makers, and understanding it prevents disappointment. A countertop ice maker is a fast ice producer, not a freezer: it rapidly makes batches of ice and drops them into an insulated basket, but that basket is not refrigerated, so the ice slowly melts if you don't use it. Cleverly, in most units the melt-water drains back into the reservoir and gets recycled to make fresh ice, so you're not wasting water and the machine keeps topping up — but the practical point is that the ice is meant to be used on demand the same day, not stockpiled frozen for hours or overnight. This makes countertop ice makers excellent for situations where you need a steady supply of fresh ice throughout a day — a party, a hot afternoon, continuously filling drinks and a cooler — because they just keep making more. But if you want a stored stockpile of ice frozen and ready for later, you need to transfer the made ice into your freezer, or rely on the freezer itself. So buy a countertop ice maker for fast, on-demand, same-day ice production, and don't expect it to hold ice frozen unused like a freezer compartment.

faqs.q: Are countertop ice makers noisy, and how much maintenance do they need?
faqs.a: Yes, they're noticeably noisy in operation, and they do need regular cleaning, though neither is a dealbreaker for most. On noise: a countertop ice maker runs a compressor (like a small fridge) plus the periodic sound of ice dropping into the basket and water cycling, so it produces a steady mechanical hum and intermittent clatter while making ice — fine in a kitchen, but potentially intrusive in a quiet open-plan living area or bedroom, so consider placement, and check reviews for noise levels if it matters to you (some models and nugget makers vary). On maintenance: like any appliance that handles water, ice makers need periodic cleaning and descaling to stay hygienic and run efficiently — mineral scale from hard water builds up and affects performance and taste, and standing water can develop mould or slime if neglected, so you should empty and dry the unit when not in use, clean the reservoir and basket regularly, and run a descaling/cleaning cycle (with a vinegar solution or the manufacturer's recommended cleaner) every few weeks to months depending on use and water hardness. Using filtered water reduces scale buildup. Neither the noise nor the maintenance is onerous — the noise is just part of how they work, and the cleaning is a simple periodic routine — but both are worth knowing before you buy.
